key_idea: Between consecutive moments when either walker passes a vertex, both move at unit speed along fixed directions, so their difference vector is linear in time and the minimum of its length on the interval has a closed form.
sketch: Place the back walker at the start and the front walker at arc length s, then sweep with two pointers: each step advances both by min(remaining length on back segment, remaining on front segment). In a step D(t)=D0+(u_front-u_back)t, so minimise |D(t)| at the clamped parameter t*=-D0.w/|w|^2 and at both ends. Stop when the front walker reaches the last vertex. O(n) with at most 2n steps. Precision: keep offsets local to the current segment instead of global arc lengths (the path can be 2.8e12 long, which would eat the 1e-4 tolerance in doubles), use long double, and treat near-simultaneous vertex arrivals with a relative epsilon; parallel directions (w=0) give constant distance. Stress-tested against dense sampling on random small paths.
